name: Poor Sleep
question: Why can I not sleep properly?
tagline: You are in bed long enough, and still wake up flat
summary: Trouble falling asleep, waking at 3am, or sleeping a full night and still feeling unrested. Poor sleep is the most common entry point into biohacking and the one with the clearest route out.
signs: Taking more than 30 minutes to fall asleep, most nights
Waking between 2am and 4am and struggling to get back down
Sleeping seven or eight hours and still needing caffeine to function
Sleep quality that collapses on weeknights and rebounds at weekends

causes.p: Your internal clock and your schedule disagree. Dark mornings and bright evenings push melatonin onset later, so you are not tired at bedtime and are exhausted at 7am.
Caffeine has a five to six hour half-life, so an afternoon coffee is measurably present at midnight. Alcohol sedates you first and fragments the second half of the night.
Core temperature must fall to initiate deep sleep. A warm bedroom is one of the most common and most fixable causes of shallow sleep.
Sleep apnoea is common, under-diagnosed and treatable. Loud snoring or waking unrefreshed after adequate hours is a reason to see a clinician, not to buy another supplement.

firstStep: Fix your wake time for seven days and get outdoor light within an hour of waking. Change nothing else. This one intervention resolves a surprising share of sleep complaints on its own.
clinical: See a clinician if you snore loudly, have been told you stop breathing in your sleep, fall asleep unintentionally during the day, or have had insomnia for more than three months. CBT-I outperforms sleep medication for chronic insomnia.

name: Brain Fog
question: Why do I feel mentally slow and unfocused?
tagline: The words are there, they just arrive late
summary: Brain fog is not a diagnosis — it is a description. Slowed recall, difficulty holding a thought, and a sense of working through fog. It almost always traces back to sleep, blood glucose, inflammation or stress load.
signs: Losing the thread mid-sentence, or reaching for common words
Reading the same paragraph three times
A sharp afternoon drop that coffee no longer fixes
Feeling clearer on holiday within two or three days

causes.p: The single largest contributor. Working memory and processing speed degrade measurably after even one short night, and the deficit accumulates without you noticing the decline.
Large post-meal glucose swings produce the classic afternoon crash. The pattern is visible within days on a continuous glucose monitor.
Systemic inflammation affects cognition. hs-CRP is the cheapest window into whether this is part of your picture.
Low vitamin D, low B12, iron deficiency and under-treated thyroid disease all present as brain fog. All are ruled in or out by standard blood tests.

firstStep: Before buying a nootropic, run a two-week sleep audit and a basic blood panel including vitamin D, B12, ferritin and thyroid function. Most brain fog resolves at that layer.
clinical: Persistent cognitive change, especially of sudden onset or alongside mood change, headache, or neurological symptoms, should be assessed by a doctor rather than self-managed.

name: Chronic Stress
question: How do I get my nervous system out of overdrive?
tagline: Wired, tired, and unable to switch off
summary: Sustained sympathetic activation — the physiological state of being permanently switched on. It shows up in HRV before it shows up in how you feel, and it degrades sleep, recovery, digestion and cognition simultaneously.
signs: A resting heart rate that has crept up several beats over months
HRV trending down against your own baseline
Waking at the same early hour with your mind already running
Feeling exhausted but unable to rest

causes.p: Stress physiology responds to perceived threat, and open loops — unfinished decisions, unspoken conflicts — keep the response active long after the event.
High training volume without adequate sleep and fuel produces the same autonomic signature as psychological stress. HRV cannot tell the two apart, which is why it is useful.
Cortisol follows a daily rhythm. Weak light signals and irregular schedules flatten that curve, which is why chronically stressed people often feel worst in the morning.
Using caffeine to override fatigue increases sympathetic tone, worsens sleep, and deepens the fatigue it was covering.

firstStep: Five minutes of slow-paced breathing at six breaths per minute, twice daily. It is free, it moves HRV within a single session, and it gives you a repeatable way to down-regulate on demand.
clinical: Persistent low mood, anxiety that interferes with daily function, or thoughts of self-harm need professional support. Breathwork and training are adjuncts, not treatments.

name: Low Energy & Fatigue
question: Why am I tired all the time?
summary: Persistent fatigue that sleep does not fix. The useful split is between fatigue caused by inadequate recovery, fatigue caused by a metabolic or nutrient problem, and fatigue that signals an undiagnosed medical condition.
signs: Needing caffeine to start and something else to stop
Energy that drops sharply 90 minutes after meals
Exercise that leaves you flattened for two days rather than energised
Fatigue that has been present for months rather than weeks

causes.p: Always check first. Adequate hours in bed is not the same as adequate sleep, and sleep apnoea is the most common overlooked cause.
If your body cannot switch efficiently between fuels, energy tracks your last meal. Mitochondrial capacity built through aerobic training is the main lever.
Iron, B12, vitamin D and magnesium deficiencies each present as fatigue and are inexpensive to test and correct.

causes.h: Thyroid, anaemia or other medical causes
causes.p: A meaningful proportion of chronic fatigue has a specific medical cause that blood work will find. This is a reason to test rather than to experiment.

firstStep: Get bloodwork before you get supplements. Full blood count, ferritin, B12, vitamin D, thyroid function and fasting insulin will explain most cases or rule out the serious ones.
clinical: Fatigue lasting more than a few weeks, or accompanied by weight change, breathlessness, fever or night sweats, needs medical assessment.

name: Slow Recovery
question: Why am I not recovering between sessions?
summary: When soreness lingers, performance plateaus and motivation drops, the problem is almost never the training programme. It is the balance between the stress applied and the recovery supplied.
signs: Soreness lasting beyond 72 hours as a routine occurrence
Resting heart rate up and HRV down across a week or more
Performance flat or declining despite consistent training
Sleep getting worse as training volume increases

causes.p: Adaptation happens during rest. Sleep is the single largest recovery input, and it is the first thing high performers cut.
Repair requires substrate. Under-eating protein or total calories reliably slows recovery regardless of what else you do.

causes.h: Too much intensity, not enough base
causes.p: Training mostly in the grey zone — too hard to recover from, too easy to drive top-end adaptation — is the most common structural error.
Cold immersion right after lifting blunts the hypertrophy signal. The tool is not wrong, the timing is.

firstStep: Track HRV on a seven-day rolling average for two weeks alongside your training log. The relationship between your hard days and your autonomic response is usually obvious once it is on one chart.
clinical: Sudden performance collapse, persistent joint pain, or recurrent injury warrants assessment by a sports medicine clinician.

name: Weight & Metabolic Drift
question: Why is my body composition changing when nothing else has?
tagline: The same habits, a different result
summary: Gradual weight gain, rising waist circumference or worsening blood markers despite unchanged behaviour. This usually reflects insulin resistance developing quietly over years, which standard annual bloodwork is poorly designed to catch.
signs: Waist circumference increasing while weight looks stable
Energy dips and hunger returning within two hours of eating
Triglycerides rising and HDL falling on routine bloodwork
Fasting glucose still normal — which is why it gets missed

causes.p: The pancreas raises insulin output for years to keep glucose normal. Fasting insulin reveals this; fasting glucose does not until much later.
Muscle is the main site of glucose disposal. Losing it with age lowers your metabolic buffer even at a stable weight.
Eating later shifts intake into the part of the day when insulin sensitivity is lowest, worsening the same food.
A single week of restricted sleep measurably reduces insulin sensitivity in healthy adults and raises appetite hormones.

firstStep: Request fasting insulin alongside your next routine bloodwork, and calculate HOMA-IR. It is inexpensive, rarely offered by default, and it reframes the whole picture.
clinical: Unintentional weight loss, excessive thirst or urination, or an abnormal glucose result should be reviewed by a doctor promptly.
